name.en: Internal Family Systems (as a parts lens)

summary.en: Describes the mind as several parts with positive intentions and a calm, curious Self that can relate to them.
summary.ru: Описывает психику как несколько частей с позитивными намерениями и спокойное, любопытное Я (Self), способное с ними соотноситься.

mentalModel.summary: Inner multiplicity is normal; parts protect; change comes through relationship, not removal.
assumptions: parts are a way of describing, not entities
every part has a positive intention
mentalModel.unitOfAnalysis: parts and their relations in a situation
mentalModel.howChangeHappens: Through relationship with parts, usually with a practitioner for deeper work.
mentalModel.languageGuidance: Use the person's own part names; never name a part for them; never call a part bad.
exploratoryQuestions: Which inner positions and needs are active right now?
What might this part be afraid would happen if it stepped back?
helperMustNot: present itself as doing IFS therapy
doesNotClaim: that an agent can provide IFS therapy
riskNotes: Exiles and burdens are trauma-adjacent material
Deep work belongs with a practitioner

toolkit.name: Noticing a part
toolkit.description: Notice, name in your own words, and ask what it wants you to know, without changing it.

representations.description: A view over Part records and part relations; never stored as a shape.

suggestionRequires: the person asked for ways of looking at inner conflict

citations.note: Shadick et al. 2013: one proof-of-concept RCT (n = 79) in rheumatoid arthritis; some outcomes sustained at one year, others not

evidence.notes: Evidence about a therapy's efficacy is not evidence that parts exist.

supports: the person's own description of inner conflict
language for inner positions the person chose

marks.owner: The Center for Self Leadership, Inc. (IFS Institute)
marks.notice: OHC features are not IFS therapy and are not IFS-certified. Internal Family Systems is the subject of US application SN 98151674 by The Center for Self Leadership, Inc. (IFS Institute), under opposition.
